task.description: Validate lib/letflow/design/req182-webhooks-routes.md against REQ-182's full acceptance criteria (docs/requirements.yaml#REQ-182). Confirm: (1) every acceptance criterion maps to a concrete, unambiguous design element -- no TBD; (2) the design contains no fenced code block reproducing real or near-real .ex file content (function bodies/composed expressions) -- signatures, @spec/@type declarations, and plain data tables only; (3) the route-to-context-function param mapping (section 3) is faithful to lib/letflow/webhooks.ex's real create/2, list/1, update/3, delete/2 @specs as they actually exist on disk today; (4) the permission-mapping claims in section 4 (including the missing-PATCH-clause finding) are independently re-verified against lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex's real, current clauses, not merely trusted from this handoff's own note; (5) the JSON allowlist (section 5) never emits secret_hash or an unscoped hmac_secret_once, and the create-response hmac_secret_once splice is confined to the one documented branch.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions with no secret supplied returns a 2xx response whose body includes hmac_secret_once carrying the plaintext secret exactly once; a subsequent GET/list of the same subscription never includes the plaintext secret or an hmac_secret_once field at all -- two explicit tests
PATCH /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/:id accepts {status: "PAUSED"} and, separately, {is_active: false}, and both result in a subscription that subsequently reads back as PAUSED via GET/list

every subscription route requires the WebhooksManage permission from REQ-069's matrix -- a caller lacking it receives 403, and a caller from a different tenant naming a real subscription id belonging to tenant A receives 404, never 403
GET /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions returns {items: [...]} with each item's target_url, event_types, status and created_at present, matching webhooksApi.list's consumer shape
DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/:id removes the subscription such that a subsequent list no longer includes it, and a second DELETE of the same id returns 404 rather than a duplicate success

the route module's moduledoc states explicitly that R-Co's webhooks.zig was not inspected in this batch (unreachable from the drafting environment) and that web/src/api/dlq.ts / web/src/types/api.ts were the binding contract instead
the design contains no fenced code block reproducing real or near-real .ex file content (function bodies/composed expressions) -- signatures, @spec/@type declarations, and plain data tables only
